picks.showTitle: Sunday Homilies with Fr. Mike Schmitz
picks.title: 09/20/26 Blind Spots: Entitlement
picks.summary: Homily from the Twenty-fifth Sunday in Ordinary Time. God does not owe me anything. Entitlement does not always look like entitlement. Sometimes, it simply feels like getting what we deserve. Whether it comes from pride or pain, we can believe that we are owed more. But grace is, by definition, an undeserved gift. The cure for entitlement is to stop asking what we are owed and to start asking what God has entrusted to us...and then receive it with gratitude. Mass Readings from September 20, 2026: Isaiah 55:6-9 Psalm 145:2-3, 8-9, 17-18Philippians 1:20c-24, 27a Matthew 20:1-16a]]>
picks.reason: Homily deeply examines entitlement and grace from a Catholic scriptural perspective.

picks.showTitle: The Rosary in a Year (with Fr. Mark-Mary Ames)
picks.title: Day 256: The Luminous Mysteries
picks.summary:
Today, we pray and meditate on the Luminous mysteries. We can draw on our mental archive, reminded of Jesus and Mary’s awareness of the couple’s needs at the Wedding Feast at Cana, and therefore our needs. In the Proclamation of the Kingdom, we’re reminded that God is here, and he is acting in the world. Finally, we can think back to the glory of the Transfiguration, God’s light visible, shining through Jesus. Today’s focus is the mysteries of the Wedding at Cana, the Proclamation of the Kingdom and Call to Repentance, and the Transfiguration. We will be praying three decades of the Rosary.

F
picks.reason: Meditation on Luminous Mysteries invites reflection on Jesus' public ministry.
